DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` misclassifies non-parseable but substantive responses as generic failures before the immune layer can diagnose `parser_yield`. The interface mismatch is between [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5481) and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3080). I reproduced this locally: two rounds of a 3000-character `parseable=False` response produced only `model_failure`, never `parser_yield`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In `process_round()`, reserve `failed=True` for delivery failures (`EMPTY`/`TIMEOUT`), so malformed-but-substantive outputs can flow into `parser_yield`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FIND: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5481) sets `failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable`, but [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3080) only emits `parser_yield` when `not failed`. A large malformed response is therefore routed away from the format-divergence detector that was designed for it.

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 5

DESCRIPTION: `false_positive_rate` is computed with a guessed denominator instead of a real round window. The approximation lives at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3418). I reproduced a concrete failure: with 11 rounds, one diagnosis from round 0, and one natural resolution in round 10, `false_positive_rate` returned `1.0` even though there were zero detections inside the last-10-round window. That can trigger bad Level-3 self-adjustments.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Stamp each diagnosis with its round and compute the denominator by exact round filtering, not by proportional tail length.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
